items.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: Pat used to get gigs at these after hour places so we worked at a place called Minnie’s Can Do, up on Fillmore Street in the Western Addition, after hours, just piano and drums.

ctx.x: Well let me ask you, the first time you made money playing the drums. Do you recall that?

Oh yeah. Let’s see. I guess it was with Patterson. Pat Patterson played the piano. And he was a good piano player, schooled in theory and harmony. And Pat used to get gigs at these after hour places so we worked at a place called Minnie’s Can Do, up on Fillmore Street in the Western Addition, after hours, just piano and drums. And I think I made two bucks. And then there was a club called the Drum Club. And it was — the building is still there but it’s under another name, that was right around the corner from the…
You didn’t get anything by her I would guess.
